newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June housing completions fell 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June housing completions fell 7.8 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year. - June May--Rev from Apr June97/96
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s: - June May--Rev from Apr June96
The department said the 1.282 million unit annual rate for overall June housing completions was the lowest since a rate of 1.203 million in December 1995.
Commerce said June completions of single-family homes fell 4.1 percent to a 1.059 million unit annual rate, the lowest since a rate of 1.050 million in February 1996.

Single-family completions fell 4.7 percent in May and rose 0.2 percent in April. The department revised those figures from a previously reported 6.8 percent decrease in May and a 0.5 percent rise in April.

June multi-family unit completions fell 22.3 percent after a revised 5.0 percent decrease in May and a revised 4.1 percent decline in April. The department revised May multi-family unit completions from a 5.2 percent drop and April from a 3.2 percent decline.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis fell in June to 109,400 units from 113,600 units in May and from 110,800 units in April. In June 1996, actual completions were reported at 125,900 units.

Privately-owned housing units under construction rose in June to a seasonally adjusted 823,000 units from 813,000 units in May and were also up from 812,000 in April. They compare with 826,000 units under construction in June 1996.
